core_claim: The mix -1, 3, -2 of three delayed copies multiplies each pure tone e^{rho u} by one number m(rho) = (1 - 2^{-rho})(2*2^{-rho} - 1), and that number is zero only on the two walls of the critical strip, so every pole inside the strip survives.
audience: A viewer who knows what a complex number and an exponential are, and who has heard of the Riemann zeta function, but who has never used a Laplace transform. They fear the words 'pole' and 'residue'. The film gives each word one picture: a pole is one pure tone, a residue is how loud the tone is. A research mathematician must also find every statement exact.
emotional_arc: Curiosity: three copies of one wiggly curve are slid and stacked. Why these delays, why these weights?
Unease: the weights sum to zero. The mix cancels things. Does it cancel the poles that the whole method needs?
Clarity: a pole is one spiral tone; a delay only turns and shrinks it; the mix is three arrows head to tail.
Revelation: the arrows close up only if q = 1 or q = 1/2, and inside the strip q is trapped strictly between those two circles.
Calm: a ribbon that never touches two rods, a landscape that touches the floor only on its walls, and one honest sentence about what this does and does not prove.

in: the definition of the mix D(u) = -g(u) + 3g(u - log 2) - 2g(u - log 4) with zero-extended delays
a pure tone e^{rho u} and its Laplace transform 1/(s - rho)
a delay by a multiplies the transform by e^{-sa}
|q| = 2^{-Re s}; the strip maps into the open annulus 1/2 < |q| < 1
the zeros of m: s = 2 pi i k / log 2 and s = 1 + 2 pi i k / log 2
the residue rule r -> m(rho) r and the floor |m| >= (1 - 2^{-sigma})(2^{1-sigma} - 1)
the worked number |m(rho_1)| = 3.984 at the first zeta zero
out: the Landau window theorem that uses the surviving poles
the definition of the observable g for a Dirichlet family and of PoleData in full
the tent weight and the prime-window criterion (they are in the paper and in the Lean file)
any claim that the Riemann hypothesis is proved: it is not

title_options: The Mix That Cannot Kill a Pole
the_big_zoom: In the q-plane station the camera dives straight down, 3x, into the right-hand side of the implication 0 < Re s < 1 => 1/2 < |q| < 1. The ember 1/2 and the ember 1 fill the frame with |q| caught between two strict inequality signs. This is the whole proof in one line: the kill points are the two ends, and q is never at an end.
